From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-call recap + next steps  integration, auth, routing

Thanks again for your time today  great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on integration and model-routing policy work: 

What we covered
- SDK setup + auth: ACME will use our JS SDK for server-side calls; service account token with scoped keys (short-lived) for production.
- Structured output & tool calling: plan to use function/tool-calling for order-extraction and inventory lookups, with a strict schema for outputs.
- Embeddings/reranker: intent to store embeddings in your existing Redis/Vector DB; we recommended a two-stage reranker (sparse retrieval -> Redwood embed + rerank).
- Model routing & policy: define latency-first fallback chain for user-facing queries (low-latency model on US region -> regional fallback -> cheaper batch model), plus cost caps and per-route quantization profiles.

Action items / owners
1) Tech deep-dive (301345m): schedule with your infra + Dev (ACME) + our infra leads (Dev + Marcus)  suggested time windows below. (Owner: Marissa)
2) Share existing auth pattern and vector store details (ACME)  we need service account pattern and where embeddings will live. (Owner: Alex/Priya)
3) Redwood to draft model-routing policy template + sample config for latency/cost SLOs and fallback chains. (Owner: Dev)
4) Integration checklist + architecture diagram (Owner: Marissa)  attached initial diagram and checklist.

Scheduling: propose Tue/Wed 10/1310/14 9:00 11:30am PT or 2:00 4:30pm PT. Please pick one and we’ll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: redwood_arch_diagram.png (high-level), integration_checklist.xlsx (post-call checklist), SOC2-summary.pdf (security snapshot)

Thanks  looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,

Thanks Marissa  helpful recap. We’re keen to move forward. A few follow-ups before the deep-dive: 

1) Auth: we use AWS IAM roles for service accounts today and prefer short-lived tokens via our STS pipeline. Can your SDK accept OIDC tokens or do we need to mint a Redwood-scoped token?

2) Embeddings: we currently store vectors in a managed Redis Vector DB (upsert via API). Would prefer not to move storage. Do you have recommendations for hybrid retrieval (local sparse index + remote vector store)?

3) Latency SLOs: our SLA target for customer-facing chat is p99 <= 350ms. Does Redwood support regional routing + warm caches to meet that?

We’re available Wed 10/14 at 10:00am PT for the deep-dive. Confirm and we’ll send invite.

Alex

Thanks Marissa  sending the artifacts below so we can be efficient on Wed. TL;DR: SDK supports OIDC tokens via token-exchange; hybrid retrieval pattern and a model-routing policy template attached.

1) Auth / SDK
- JS SDK accepts Bearer tokens; we support a token-exchange endpoint (OIDC -> short-lived Redwood service token). See snippet: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <OIDC_TOKEN>" https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/auth/exchange -> returns short_lived_token. Recommend 15m TTL tokens for production.

2) Hybrid retrieval pattern (code snippet summary)
- Step A: local sparse retrieval (FAISS) to filter ~200 candidate docs
- Step B: bulk top-k call to ACME Redis vector DB (your endpoint) to get top 50 vector candidates
- Step C: call Redwood embed + reranker endpoint to rank top 50 with context (we offer batch rerank for efficiency)
- Perf estimates: on our infra, typical end-to-end rerank (50 docs) = ~120180ms additional CPU time; dependent on embedding dim and network RTT to your vector store.

3) Model routing & policy (attached as redwood_model_routing_example.yaml in the architecture note)
- Example policy highlights (plain text):
  * Route: chat-ui
  * Primary: gpt-small-latency (us-west) with KV caching and continuous-batching disabled for p99 SLO
  * Fallback: gpt-medium-cost (us-west) for degraded latency; regional fallback to gpt-small-latency (eu-west) for EU users
  * Cost caps: per-route daily token budget and per-request max quantization level (int8 for bulk background ops)
  * Automatic warm-cache: pre-warming hook for high-frequency user cohorts during peak hours

Attachments included below: architecture note (redwood_arch_diagram.png), integration checklist, and model-routing example YAML. I attached a short SOC2 summary for security questions.

Next steps: I’ve scheduled the deep-dive with ACME for Wed 10/14 10:00am PT  calendar invite sent. I’ll bring Marcus for perf and kernel selection questions.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
